game.name: Eight Ball Deluxe
changelog: v1.1 (2026-04-12): Added lamp_code and aux_board fields to all 88 lamps. Added strobe_signals and return_signals to switch_matrix. Added sound_commands section with 47 EBD voice/effect commands. Lamp code is the MC14514 decoder address used for bus-side lamp decode.

notes: BCD codes 1-9 map to decoder outputs Q1-Q9 via U2 74L154.
Direct-drive solenoids Q15-Q19 are not decoder-controlled.
Multi-drop connectors: some transistors drive multiple connector pins simultaneously.
Solenoid supply is 43V — omit for bench logic testing. Decoder outputs can be verified at logic level without coil voltage present.

VERSION CORRECTION (2026-03-30): ALL BCD codes corrected from driver board schematic. Previous versions incorrectly used transistor number as BCD code. The 74L154 decoder on the AS-2518-16 driver board has crossover wiring between decoder outputs and transistor bases. BCD code = decoder output label (1-based), NOT transistor number. Decoder output 12 does not exist (gap in numbering).

decoder_map.description: 74L154 decoder output to transistor mapping — SCHEMATIC VERIFIED 2026-03-30
decoder_map.note: BCD code corresponds to decoder output label, NOT transistor number. Crossover wiring exists.

outputs.12: NOT USED — gap in decoder output numbering

notes: SCR numbers (Q01-Q60) refer to lamp driver SCRs on the lamp driver board (AS-2518-23), not solenoid transistors.
Connector prefix A5 = lamp driver board. Connector prefix A9 = MPU board lamp matrix outputs.
tr_type MCR-106 = standard lamp SCR. 2N5060 = lower current SCR for lower-power lamps.
Some SCRs drive multiple lamps (shared Q number across multiple connector/description entries).
Thumper Bumper Left lamp (Q06, A9J2-6) corresponds to Left Thumper Bumper solenoid (Sol 4, Q5). Useful correlation for fault diagnosis.
Commands sent to Squawk & Talk board as 4-bit nibbles, lower nibble first then upper.
Byte values here are the reconstructed full command (lower nibble | upper nibble << 4).
Decode: observe U11 PB write, extract lower nibble, wait for next write, extract lower nibble as upper, combine.
Multiple quoted strings on one command indicate random selection by CPU.

commands.0x0F: Sound effect then: 'Woops Too Much English' or 'Too Bad You Scratch'
commands.0x55: You've got the Solids / Shooting Solids
commands.0x56: You've got the Stripes / Shooting Stripes
commands.0x5B: You've got the Deluxe Nice Shot
